steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Ore
form.label: a few grams in every tonne

steps.text: The six platinum-group metals occur together. Most lie in a few thin layers of the Bushveld Complex in South Africa, an ancient body of once-molten rock, with more in Zimbabwe's Great Dyke. In Russia and Canada they come as a by-product of nickel and copper sulphide ore. Iridium is a trace even within this group.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: The South African reefs are about a metre thick and are followed more than a kilometre underground. Miners drill and blast the narrow seam and haul the rock to the shaft. It is deep, hot and labour-intensive work.

steps.title: Concentrate
steps.text: The ore is milled to powder and floated. The platinum-group metals follow the nickel and copper sulphide grains into a concentrate that is a small fraction of the rock mined.

steps.title: Smelt
steps.text: An electric furnace melts the concentrate. Silicates leave as slag and the metals collect in a matte of nickel, copper and iron sulphide. A converter burns off the iron. The nickel and copper are then leached away for sale, leaving a residue rich in precious metals.

steps.title: Refine
steps.text: The residue is dissolved in hydrochloric acid and chlorine. One by one the metals are pulled out by solvent extraction, precipitation and distillation, in a refinery where material can spend weeks or months. Iridium is one of the minor metals and the last to dissolve; it is recovered from the residue after the others.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Iridium powder is melted and worked into crucibles, alloyed into spark-plug tips, or coated as oxide onto titanium anodes and electrolyser membranes.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Iridium is the most corrosion-resistant metal. Iridium crucibles grow the crystals for LEDs and lasers. Iridium oxide is the anode catalyst in PEM electrolysers that make green hydrogen, and well under ten tonnes are mined each year, which caps how fast those can be built.
steps.india: All imported. The green hydrogen mission and electronics create the demand.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Crucibles and anodes are returned and refined when they wear out, so industrial iridium circulates. Recovery from electrolysers will matter as they age.
steps.india: Hindustan Platinum and other refiners recover platinum-group metals from spent catalysts. A Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme (2025) covers catalytic converters.
